sentences: Can food be three thousand years old?
Yes, it can!
Scientists in Egypt found old pots in a tomb.
There was honey in the pots.
The honey was three thousand years old.
And it was good to eat!
Why does honey never go bad?
Honey has got very little water.
Bacteria can't live without water.
Honey is also very sweet.
So it stays fresh for a very long time.
Bees make honey from flowers.
One bee makes only a little honey.
So a spoon of honey is hard work.
Next time you eat honey, remember the old tomb!
Dana can't see the path.
There is snow everywhere.
It is cold and the sun is going down.
Her dog Bars is with her.
“Where is the village?”
she says.
Bars stops.
He looks at Dana.
Then he walks to the left.
Dana goes with him.
They walk and walk.
Her hands are very cold.
Then she sees a light!
It is a small house.
An old man opens the door.
He has got hot tea.
“Your dog is clever,” he says.
“This is the only house on the mountain.”
Dana hugs Bars.
Dogs can smell a house from far away.
Nobody lives in the house at number 12.
But every night a light is in the window.
Every night, at ten o'clock.
Who is there?
Timur and his sister Aida want to know.
On Friday they go to the house.
The door is open.
The house is dark and quiet.
They go up the stairs.
Then — click!
The light is on.
Aida laughs.
On the table there is an old lamp.
On the lamp there is a big grey cat.
The cat sleeps on the button every night.
Mystery solved!
Now the cat lives with Timur and Aida.
The first man in space went up from Kazakhstan.
His name was Yuri Gagarin.
The date was 12 April 1961.
The place was Baikonur, in the Kazakh steppe.
The name of the rocket was Vostok.
Gagarin was in space for 108 minutes.
He saw the Earth from above.
“The Earth is blue,” he said.
Then he was back at home.
He was a hero.
Today Baikonur is still a big space centre.
Rockets go up from there every year.
People from many countries go to space.
They go from the steppe of Kazakhstan.
And the first was Gagarin, in 1961.
There is a small helicopter on Mars.
Its name is Ingenuity.
It is very small — only 1.
8 kilograms.
On 19 April 2021 it went up.
It was the first flight on another planet.
Flying on Mars is very hard.
The air on Mars is very thin.
So the helicopter has got very fast blades.
It can fly for only a few minutes.
It can't fly for a long time.
People made Ingenuity for five flights.
But it made 72 flights!
It found the best way for the robot Perseverance.
In January 2024 the helicopter had an accident.
Now it stands on Mars and doesn't fly.
But it made history.
Some birds fly and don't stop for ten months!
The bird is the common swift.
It is small, dark and very fast.
It eats in the air.
It drinks in the air.
It even sleeps in the air.
How can a bird sleep and fly?
Scientists think the swift sleeps for short moments.
It goes very high in the evening.
Then it comes down slowly.
One part of its brain sleeps.
The other part does not sleep.
The swift only stops to have babies.
Its nest is under a roof.
The babies learn to fly.
Then the family goes back into the sky.
Look up in summer.
Maybe a swift is over your head now.
In 2002 William was fourteen.
His home was a village in Malawi, Africa.
That year there was no rain.
There was no food and no money.
There was no money for school.
But there was a library in the village.
William found a book about wind and electricity.
The book was in English.
William saw the pictures and he had an idea.
William made a windmill from old things.
He had a bicycle, wood and plastic.
People said, “He is crazy!”
But the windmill made electricity.
There was light in his house!
Today William helps children in Africa to study.
One book, one idea, one boy.
Where do apples come from?
Not from your shop.
Not from your garden.
Apples come from the mountains near Almaty, in Kazakhstan!
Scientists found this with the help of DNA.
Almaty comes from the Kazakh word alma — “apple”.
There are wild apple trees in the mountains today.
Some trees are very old and very big.
The apples are red, yellow and green.
Almaty has got a famous apple: the Aport.
It is very big.
One apple can be half a kilogram!
People in Almaty are proud of it.
In autumn there is an apple festival.
Come and try one.
The blue whale is very, very big.
It is big like a bus.
No animal in the world is so big.
Its heart is big too — like a small car!
A whale goes down deep in the sea.
Then its heart is very slow.
It goes only two times in a minute!
Then the whale comes up.
Its heart goes fast again.
The blue whale eats very small animals — krill.
It eats four tonnes of krill in a day.
Its tongue is heavy like an elephant.
But it can't eat a person.
Its throat is too small!
“Don't go into the cave,” says Grandpa.
But Arman and Lena have got a torch.
And they have got a question: what is inside?
The cave is dark and wet.
Water drops from the roof.
The children walk slowly.
Then the torch goes off!
It is very dark.
Lena can't see her hand.
“Don't move,” says Arman.
“Wait.”
After a minute they can see a small light.
It comes from a hole in the wall.
They go to the light.
It is a way out!
They are on the hill, in the sun.
There is an old picture on the wall.
It is a horse.
Somebody was here a long time ago.
Every morning the bread is not there.
Grandma buys bread in the evening.
She puts it on the table.
In the morning — no bread!
“Who eats my bread?”
she says.
Grandma has got a plan.
On Sunday night she doesn't go to bed.
She sits in the dark kitchen.
She waits.
At two o'clock she hears a noise.
Somebody is in the kitchen!
Grandma turns on the light.
And she sees…
her parrot, Kesha!
The parrot's cage is open.
Kesha is on the table with the bread.
“Good morning!”
says the parrot.
Grandma laughs.
Now she closes the cage every night.
And the bread is always there.
In 2008 scientists went into a cave in Armenia.
It was dark and cold.
In the ground they found a shoe.
It was a small leather shoe with a string.
It was 5,500 years old!
The shoe was not broken.
Why?
The cave was dry and cool.
There was grass in the shoe.
So the shoe was like new.
It is size 37 — a woman's size today.
Whose shoe was it?
A man's or a woman's?
Nobody knows.
But we know one thing.
Five thousand years ago people had shoes.
They had strings and warm feet.
Now the shoe is in a museum in Yerevan.
The first website in the world is still online.
It is very simple.
There are no pictures, no colours, no videos.
Only black text and blue links.
And it is very important.
Tim Berners-Lee from England made it in 1991.
His job was at CERN in Switzerland.
Scientists there had a problem.
They had a lot of information on many computers.
Tim had an idea: links between all the pages.
The idea was the World Wide Web.
It is the “www” in every address.
Tim's idea was free for everybody.
He said: “This is for the whole world.”
Today there are more than a billion websites.
And the first was one page of text.
Sea otters sleep in the water.
But the sea moves.
How do they stay together?
They hold hands!
A mother and a baby.
Or a group of friends.
They sleep on their backs, hand in hand.
Otters have got a trick, too.
They put sea plants — kelp — around their bodies.
The kelp is like a bed.
So the otter doesn't go away in the night.
Sea otters have got very thick fur.
No animal has got fur like this.
They also use tools.
An otter has got a favourite stone.
It keeps it in a pocket under its arm.
It opens shells with the stone.
Clever, right?
At seven o'clock Roza Apa opens her laptop.
She is seventy-eight.
She is learning English.
“Why?”
people ask.
“Because my grandson is in London,” she says.
Roza Apa doesn't study alone.
Her neighbour, a girl of ten, helps her.
They read short texts.
They listen to songs.
They laugh a lot.
When Roza Apa makes a mistake, she says: “Again!”
Last month her grandson had a birthday.
Roza Apa said “Happy birthday!”
on video.
She said it in English!
Her grandson was very happy.
Now Roza Apa has got a new dream.
It is a trip to London.
“I am old,” she says.
“But my brain is young.”
Thousands of people.
One small street.
And more than one hundred tonnes of tomatoes.
This is La Tomatina — a tomato fight in Spain.
It is in the town of Buñol, near Valencia.
It is on the last Wednesday of August.
Trucks come with the tomatoes.
At eleven o'clock the fight starts.
People throw tomatoes for one hour.
Everybody is red!
There are rules.
You can't throw hard tomatoes.
Please break the tomato in your hand first.
After the fight, water washes the streets.
And the tomatoes?
They are cheap tomatoes for the festival.
They are not for eating.
Do you want to go?
